beats.say: Type-C is C11 with the types C is missing: variants checked by match, distinct types for ids and units, generics, and errors as values.
Its compiler takes the same command line as cc, turns Type-C into readable C, and hands that to your normal C compiler.
Every C11 file is already valid Type-C, so a project can adopt it one file at a time. It's early, with much of the language still unbuilt.
